To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the diterpenoid compounds isolated from A. sinchiangense showed significant antitumour and antibacterial activities, and the new diterpenoid compound 1 showed the most potent antitumor and antitubercular activities among them.
sinchiangensines A and B are the first C19-diterpene alkaloids with significant antitumor and antibiotic activities.
the new diterpenoid sinchiangensin A was isolated from Aconitum root, and its structure and biological activities are reported for the first time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation, structure elucidation, and biological activity of the new diterpenoid sinchiangensin A, and the first report on the potential antitumor activity and antibacterial activity of the diterpenoid from the genus Aconitum.
the isolation of diterpenoid alakoids from A. sinchiangense, which may be used in the future as potential antitumour and antibacterial drugs.
the chemical investigation of A. sinchiangense and the discovery of the bioactivities of its diterpenoid constituents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the root of A. sinchiangense is a promising source of new antitumour and antibacterial agents.
the diterpenoid alakaloids from A. sinchiangense have significant antitumor activity and antibacterial activity.
sinchiangensines A and B, as well as their known analogues 3, 5 and 7 are potential antitumor or antibacterial diterpene alkaloids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diterpenoid alcaloids isolated from A. sinchiangense root barks have significant antitumor and antituberculosis activities, which might provide new insights for the development of new antitumor and anti-tuberculosis drugs.
the root barks extract of A. sinchiangense has potential antitumor activities and its active ingredients may be the diterpenoid compounds.

sinchiangensines A-C and 3-6 were the first report of the diterpenoid constituents from this plant, and the antitumor and antimicrobial activities of sinchiangensins A-C and 2-6 were the firstly reported for these compounds.

the C19-diterpene alkaloids isolated from Aconitum species are potential antitumor agents.
the diterpenoid sinchiangensines A and B are potential antitumor agents.
the C19-diterpene alkaloids are a promising source for the development of new anticancer and antibacterial drugs.
